completion_promises.criterion_text: LifecycleBridge.recover_in_flight() (stub from T2) is implemented. Iterates BridgeRegistry.list_active(); for each entry, schedules an asyncio task that reconnects with the persisted Last-Event-ID.
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented RecoveryRunner.run() in src/forge/lifecycle_bridge/recovery.py. The method calls BridgeRegistry.list_active() (line 332), then schedules one asyncio.create_task per entry (lines 354-360) that reconnects via the recovery_source with entry.last_event_id (passed as Last-Event-ID, line 487). Tested in TestInBufferReplay::test_replay_publishes_3_envelopes_and_deletes_row which asserts source.calls[0]['last_event_id'] == 'evt-3'. The pre-existing LifecycleBridge.recover_in_flight() returns the registry list for forge status --in-flight (T12); the boot-time orchestration lives in RecoveryRunner to keep the bridge focused on SSE-attached lifecycle while the runner owns boot-time orchestration (SRP).

completion_promises.criterion_text: Idempotency: each registry row tracks published_lifecycles (set of envelope subjects already on the wire — e.g. {'build-started'}); the SSE observer's publish path checks this set before publishing and skips already-published transitions. Persisted as a JSON-encoded TEXT column.
completion_promises.evidence: Added published_lifecycles TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' column to lifecycle_bridge_registry via idempotent migration (_ensure_published_lifecycles_column with PRAGMA table_info guard). Added BridgeRegistryEntry.published_lifecycles: frozenset[str] field with JSON encode/decode helpers in bridge_registry.py. Added BridgeRegistry.mark_published() which appends inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. RecoveryRunner._publish_with_idempotency() marks BEFORE publish (line 599 of recovery.py) and the recovery flow checks already_published set before invoking publish (line 466). Tested in TestPublishedLifecyclesIdempotency::test_already_published_subject_is_skipped.

completion_promises.criterion_text: When the SSE server rejects the Last-Event-ID (e.g. HTTP 410 or empty replay window), the bridge falls back to runs.get once to determine current state. If terminal, publish the terminal envelope and ack. If still running, restart the SSE stream with Last-Event-ID=0.
completion_promises.evidence: RecoveryRunner._recover_one() catches LastEventIdRejected and dispatches to _sweep_via_runs_get() which calls self._runs_client.get(thread_id, run_id) exactly once (line 511 of recovery.py). When status is terminal it opens a fresh SSE stream with last_event_id=None; the translator emits the terminal payload through the same publish path (single emit-site invariant preserved). When status is running, the same fresh stream resumes per-stage observation. Tested in TestOutOfBufferSweep::test_410_rejection_publishes_terminal_via_fresh_stream (asserts runs_client.get.assert_awaited_once_with) and test_410_rejection_with_running_status_resumes_fresh_stream.

completion_promises.criterion_text: recover_in_flight() is called from forge serve startup before the consumer starts processing new build-queued envelopes. Recovery completes within 30s for ≤10 in-flight builds.
completion_promises.evidence: DEFAULT_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS = 30.0 enforced via asyncio.wait_for in RecoveryRunner.run() (line 365 of recovery.py). On timeout, pending tasks are cancelled and a failure_reason='budget-exceeded' is recorded (line 372-376). The convenience entrypoint run_recovery_at_boot() exposes a single seam for forge serve startup wiring. The pre-startup-ordering invariant is locked in by TestPreStartupOrdering::test_recovery_completes_before_subsequent_step which asserts ['recovery-start', 'recovery-end', 'consumer-fetch'] ordering. The 30s budget is asserted by TestRecoveryBudget::test_default_budget_is_30_seconds and the cancellation behaviour by test_budget_exceeded_cancels_pending_tasks.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Build-started is not re-published if it was already published pre-restart (the regression scenario explicitly listed).
completion_promises.evidence: TestBuildStartedNotRePublished::test_build_started_skipped_then_terminal_published seeds the registry with published_lifecycles=frozenset({'build-started'}), drives a replay containing a build-started AND a build-complete, and asserts 'build-started' NOT in published subjects while 'build-complete' IS published. The regression is locked at the recovery.py level (line 466 in _replay_in_buffer: 'if subject in already_published: skipped.append(subject); ... continue').

completion_promises.criterion_text: Multi-build restart: 3 concurrent recoveries work without interference; each updates its own registry row.
completion_promises.evidence: RecoveryRunner.run() creates one asyncio.Task per active registry entry and gathers them with asyncio.wait_for (lines 354-368 of recovery.py). Each task only touches its own feature_id row via the registry's BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialisation. TestMultiBuildRecovery::test_three_concurrent_recoveries_all_complete seeds 3 entries (FEAT-M1/M2/M3), drives concurrent recovery, and asserts all 3 entries deleted plus each build saw its own ['build-started', 'build-complete'] sequence with correct payload.feature_id correlation. The _async_iterator helper yields after asyncio.sleep(0) to force interleaving so the test exercises real concurrency.
